name: Hakka Chinese
variety: Sixian Hakka of Taiwan (Northern Sixian, Miaoli), which is the variety that eSpeak NG's tone values, its sandhi rule and its Pha̍k-fa-sṳ input correspond to; Meixian (Guangdong) values are given for comparison
sources: Hashimoto, Mantaro J. (1973). The Hakka Dialect: A Linguistic Study of its Phonology, Syntax and Lexicon. Cambridge University Press.
Lee, Wai-Sum & Zee, Eric (2009). Hakka Chinese. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 39(1), 107-111.
Chung, Raung-fu (2004). Taiwan Kejia yuyin daolun [An introduction to the sounds of Taiwan Hakka]. Taipei: Wunan.
Ministry of Education, Taiwan (2012). Kejiayu pinyin fang'an [Hakka romanisation scheme], with tone values for the Sixian, Hailu, Dapu, Raoping and Zhao'an varieties.
Chen, Matthew Y. (2000). Tone Sandhi: Patterns across Chinese Dialects. Cambridge University Press.
contrasts: aspirated versus unaspirated in stops and affricates; no voiced stops
three final nasals m n ŋ and three final stops p t k, all kept (unlike Mandarin)
four tones in open and nasal-final syllables and two in checked syllables
apical (central) vowel ɨ against i after the sibilants
allophony: ts tsʰ s are alveolo-palatal [tɕ tɕʰ ɕ] before i in Sixian; Hailu and some other varieties have a separate postalveolar series
ŋ is palatal [ɲ] before i (written ngi)
v is a weakly fricated labiodental, often an approximant [ʋ]
final p t k are unreleased
the vowel written ṳ in Pha̍k-fa-sṳ (ii in the Ministry scheme) is an apical or central unrounded vowel [ɨ], found only after ts tsʰ s
zero-initial syllables beginning with i have a palatal glide onset, with friction in some varieties
syllable_structure: (C)(G)V(C) plus tone, where G is i or u and the coda is one of m n ŋ p t k or an offglide; or a syllabic nasal plus tone
phonotactics: codas are limited to m n ŋ p t k and offglides
checked syllables (ending in p t k) carry only the two entering tones, yinru and yangru
ɨ occurs only after the sibilants ts tsʰ s

stress.rule: Every syllable carries a lexical tone; no stress placement rule is described.
stress.cues: not documented in the sources used

rhythm.notes: No instrumental rhythm study of Sixian Hakka is known to the compiler; the class is given by analogy with other southern Sinitic languages and should be treated as low confidence.

length.notes: No length contrast. Vowels in checked syllables are short.

intonation.declarative: lexical tones are kept, with declination; sentence-final particles carry much of the sentence-type meaning
intonation.yes_no_question: marked mainly by a final particle or by A-not-A form; instrumental descriptions of the melody are lacking
intonation.continuation: not documented in the sources used
intonation.notes: Hakka intonation is poorly documented; these entries are general and of low confidence.

tone.confidence_notes: high for the Sixian citation values, which are the official Ministry of Education values; medium for durations and phonation

inventory.name: tone 1, yinping 陰平 (Pha̍k-fa-sṳ circumflex, â)
inventory.connected_speech: 11 (low level, like yangping) before yinping 24, qusheng 55 and yangru 5; 24 elsewhere

inventory.name: tone 2, yangping 陽平 (Pha̍k-fa-sṳ grave, à)
tone 3, shangsheng 上聲 (Pha̍k-fa-sṳ acute, á)
tone 4, qusheng 去聲 (Pha̍k-fa-sṳ unmarked, a)
tone 5, yinru 陰入 (Pha̍k-fa-sṳ unmarked with final p t k, ak)
inventory.phonation: modal, cut off by the unreleased final stop

inventory.name: tone 6, yangru 陽入 (Pha̍k-fa-sṳ vertical line above with final p t k, a̍k)
inventory.phonation: modal, cut off by the unreleased final stop

sandhi: Sixian (Northern, Miaoli): yinping 24 becomes low level 11, the same as yangping, before a syllable with yinping 24, qusheng 55 or yangru 5 (before the tones that are or end high); it stays 24 before yangping 11, shangsheng 31 and yinru 2
the other Sixian tones do not change
other varieties have different and larger sets of rules (Hailu, Meixian); they are not described here
tone.neutral_tone: no neutral tone comparable to Mandarin is described for Sixian
tone.notes: Meixian (Hashimoto 1973; Lee & Zee 2009) differs: yinping 44, yangping 11, shangsheng 31, qusheng 52 or 53, yinru 1 or 21, yangru 5. The combination low rising yinping 24 with high level qusheng 55 is what identifies eSpeak NG's table as Sixian. Hailu, the other main Taiwan variety, has seven tones (53, 55, 24, 11, 33, 5, 2) and roughly mirror-image pitch values. No published F0 values are given here.

phonation: no phonation contrast; aspiration only in stops and affricates
checked syllables end in an unreleased stop

problems: only Pha̍k-fa-sṳ romanisation can be read: hak_list holds nothing but numerals, so Hakka written in Han characters is not spoken, although the language is flagged as using ideographs
the Sixian sandhi rule is applied only inside one written word (syllables joined by hyphens or written together): thiên-kông becomes 11 24 but thiên kông with a space keeps 24 24
no sentence intonation and no declination: CalcPitches_Tone() in src/libespeak-ng/intonation.c ignores the clause type, and a question gives the same audio as a statement
the checked tones are not short in themselves: every vowel has length 250, and the checked syllable is shortened only by the time taken by the final stop (vowel about 210 ms against 280 ms measured)
final p t k have a weak release burst after about 40 ms of closure, where Hakka has unreleased stops
rule gaps: the rhyme ie with the yangru mark is not covered (ngie̍t is misparsed), and chhṳ is given the alveolo-palatal affricate that belongs before i

the tone table uses a different pitch scale from the other tone languages (20 to 100 instead of 10 to 50), giving about 81 to 122 Hz at the default voice pitch (about 7 semitones, measured); this is wider than eSpeak's Mandarin and Cantonese but still narrower than natural speech
good: the tone table carries the Sixian values as IPA tone letters (24, 11, 31, 55, 2, 5) and the pitch targets match them
the Sixian yinping sandhi is implemented in C, in CalcPitches_Tone() in src/libespeak-ng/intonation.c: tone 1 becomes tone 2 before tones 1, 4 and 6
aspirated and unaspirated stops and affricates, v, the palatal nasal, the apical vowel and the three syllabic nasals are all present

notes: The status of the voice in eSpeak NG is 'testing'. Pha̍k-fa-sṳ marks tone by diacritics: circumflex yinping, grave yangping, acute shangsheng, no mark qusheng or yinru, vertical line above yangru.
